comments.author: @CentrelRole
comments.text: No. They cannot climb trees. This is false. Tell me how an animal like that can climb a tree.
comments.replyText: Actually, it's true! Researchers from the University of Tennessee documented alligators climbing trees up to 6 feet high. They use their powerful tails for balance and sharp claws to grip bark. It's mostly younger, lighter gators that do it — they climb to bask in the sun and survey their territory. Nature is wild!
